problem:
The function $y=f(x)$ satisfies the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=y-x.
$$

Given that the point $(0,0)$ lies on the graph of $y=f(x),$ which of the following statements are true?

- $(0,0)$ is a stationary point of the function $f$
- $(0,0)$ is a local minimum point of the function $f$
- $(0,0)$ is an inflection point of the function $f$

feedback.problem:
The function $y=f(x)$ satisfies the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=3y+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

 

Given that the point $P(\pi ,1)$ lies on the graph of the function, evaluate $\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}$ at $P.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find an expression for the second derivative, we differentiate the equation with respect to $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3y+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3y)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =3\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =3\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute the given expression for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ into the above and simplify the resulting expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =3(3y+2\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =9y+6\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the coordinates of our point into the above expression for the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}|}_{(\pi ,1)} & ={(9y+6\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x)|}_{(\pi ,1)} \\  & =9(1)+6\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ) \\  & =9-2 \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$
